items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 63
notes: John Vos gave a presentation with a brief overview of the proposal, including the site context and the planning framework. He then responded to questions of Council.
Kristen Barisdale, GSP Group gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development, including the site context and site plans. She then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 72
notes: Kaitlyn Bisch gave a presentation providing Council with an overview of the application, including the site context, planning framework, and the conceptual floorplans. She then responded to questions of Council. Ron Ormson also responded to questions of Council.

Brandon Simon, The Planning Partnership gave a presentation further outlining the application, including the transit connections and the reuse of the existing building. He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: General Amendments to Zoning By-law
notes: Prepared By: Ashlyn Fox and Kaitlyn Bisch

Ashlyn Fox gave a presentation outlining the proposed general amendments, including changes made by Council decisions and Provincial regulations, and hospital use definitions. She then responded to questions of Council. Kaitlyn Bisch also responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Wright had a question about the pavilion booking systems for Waterloo Park and waste management. Robin Milne provided a background of the issues relating to booking options and waste.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roach mentioned that on Wednesday, July 15, scholarship applications close with the Canadian Caribbean Association of Waterloo Region.

Councillor Vasic gave a shoutout to the Neighbourhoods team for their support in hosting the first ever neighbourhood picnic in Dunvegan Park on June 20. The feedback from the community was great and about 60 people came to the event.
Councillor Vasic also recognized that the KW Palestine Festival was yesterday, July 12, in Kitchener, with cultural celebrations, good food, and vendors.

Councillor Hanmer announced that Waterloo is hosting the Ontario Summer Games, along with other cities in the Waterloo Region, during the last week of July, with over 4500 coaches and athletes coming out for that.

Councillor Roe also gave a shoutout to the Neighbourhoods team for their support during the Beechwood North Canada Day celebration, which featured an artist on site and great activities for the children.

Councillor Roe also attended an event for World Refugee Day on Friday, June 19, where Reception House brought some new arrivals who had only been here for a few days. It’s the focus of the Community Coalition on Refugee and Immigrant Concerns (CCORIC) to make people feel welcome and recognize contributions to the community.
Councillor Wright highlighted the Community Picnic on July 1 in Waterloo Park. The weather was intense, but she gave props to the team for persevering through hot weather, wind and rain.
Councillor Wright also mentioned that Kultrun was this past weekend, July 10-12, held by Neruda Arts, which reinforces the message that everyone is welcome here and features excellent music.
Councillor Wright finished by mentioning that Afro Vibes is unfolding this coming week, in Waterloo and Kitchener.

motions.item_title: Disposition of Part of Sunview Street
motions.text: 1. The Council approve report IPPW2026-045. 2. That Council declare as surplus the segment of Sunview Street (formerly Unger Street) located south of Seagram Drive as shown on Map 1 to IPPW2026-045, legally described as: UNGER ST PL 507 CITY OF WATERLOO BEING SUNVIEW ST ABUTTING LT 25 & 29 PL 507; WATERLOO, being PIN 22377-0164(LT) save and except a 3.048 metre widening to Seagram Drive (the “Lands”). 3. That Council approve the stop up and closure of the Lands as a municipal highway pursuant to section 34 of the Municipal Act. 4. That Council authorize the Chief Administrative Officer and City Solicitor to prepare an Agreement of Purchase and Sale to convey the Lands to Wilfrid Laurier University (“Laurier”) substantially consistent with the following terms: a) for the nominal sum of $2.00 plus transfer, administrative and legal costs incurred by the City of Waterloo; b) a condition that obligates Laurier, if it no longer has an interest in the Lands, to reconvey the Lands to the City free and clear of encumbrances and in a safe and usable condition for the nominal sum of $2.00; and c) the transfer of a minimum 750 square metres of land from Wilfrid Laurier University to The Corporation of the City of Waterloo for highway widening purposes, to the satisfaction of the City’s Chief Administrative Officer, for the nominal sum of $2.00. Further: • the lands shall be free and clear of encumbrances • all costs including reference plans and legal costs shall be borne by Laurier • form and content of all transfer related documents shall be to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor d) a condition that obligates Laurier to consent to the relocation of easement WR833293 and the right-of-way as in Instrument No. 1126672 if required by The Corporation of the City of Waterloo, to permit the relocation and/or realignment of the westerly driveway to Laurier Stadium, provided further that: i. any such relocation shall constitute a relocation only, and not a discharge or removal, of the easement and right-of- way, unless otherwise agreed to by the parties; and ii. equivalent or improved access rights are maintained at all times. For clarity of recommendation d.)ii., the relocated easement and right-of-way shall maintain all existing functional requirements of the existing driveway, including maintaining uninterrupted fire route access to Laurier Stadium, in a manner satisfactory to The Corporation of the City of Waterloo and applicable fire safety authorities. 5. That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute the Agreement of Purchase and Sale and all other documents necessary to complete the transactions, subject to the approval of such documents by the City Solicitor.
